# Ramirez Hospitality Group
> Operator-led revenue and opening consultancy for independent hotels, motels and inns with fewer than 50 rooms. Based in Palm Springs, California. Working nationwide.

## About

Ramirez Hospitality Group (RHG) was founded by Adam Ramirez, a Palm Springs hotel operator. The track record: 10+ years · 50+ hospitality properties · 20% average revenue lift. Eight hotels opened from concept to ribbon-cutting, four repositioned, $10M+ in annual hotel revenue managed, six funded feasibility projects. Every price is flat and published, nothing is on commission, and everything RHG builds lives in the client's own accounts.

Properties opened, repositioned, or run include: The Paloma Resort, Twist Palm Springs, Limón Palm Springs, Sands Hotel & Spa, The Stardust, Dunes Palm Springs, The Creekstone Inn, Town & Desert Hospitality, Bellevue Oasis, Float Palm Springs, Saguaro Hotel.

Press: Travel & Leisure, Condé Nast Traveler, Forbes, Modernism Magazine.

## The three offers

### 1. The Modern Hotel Audit (free)
Where every client who runs a hotel starts. The property is scored out of 100 across seven areas (reputation and rate-worthiness, direct booking engine, distribution and channel health, technology and automation, demand capture, pricing and rate strategy, whole-property yield). Every finding is priced in dollars with the evidence behind it. The two most valuable fixes are written out in full and are the owner's to keep whether or not they hire RHG. Every finding is tagged to the cheapest subscription plan that captures it, so the plan decision is arithmetic. The catch, in full: at the end RHG asks whether the owner wants help fixing the three lowest scores.
Call to action: Book The Modern Hotel Audit. https://ramirezhospitality.com/audit

### 2. The Subscription (revenue management)
Your prices set every day. Your booking sites worked. Your groups priced right. The revenue department every big hotel has, for a hotel with fewer than 50 rooms, run by an operator inside rules the owner sets. Three plans, flat and published, nothing on commission:
- Essentials: $1,250 a month. Your prices, set every day. For one property, rooms bringing in roughly $300,000 to $750,000 a year. Rates reviewed and updated daily inside floors and ceilings the owner approves; events and holidays priced ahead; a weekly rate-parity check; booking-site listings scored and fixed; the direct-booking starter kit; a one-page monthly report and a 30-minute monthly call; re-scored against the audit on a written schedule.
- Growth: $2,000 a month. Your whole revenue system, run for you. For one or two properties, rooms bringing in roughly $600,000 to $1.2 million a year. Everything in Essentials plus a named revenue manager, every-morning pickup review, a rolling forecast and yearly budget, booking sites worked as a cost line, booking engine and Google hotel listing set up for direct bookings, group-ready pricing and quote templates, monthly segment reporting, a 60-minute call every two weeks.
- In-House: $5,000 a month. A revenue manager on your team, without the payroll. For rooms bringing in $1.2 million and up a year, 30-plus rooms, or meaningful group and event business. By application. Everything in Growth plus daily work inside the owner's own Duetto account five days a week, a weekly call and weekly report, a landing page and Google Ads set up and taught, the group offer and rate card, sales contract templates, group and negotiated-business listings, the owner taught to answer RFPs and when to say no, quarterly on-site visits (travel and accommodations provided by the client). A full-time salary pays for a seat; the property needs 25 to 30 hours a month of the actual work.
Terms: no setup fee. Four-month initial term on Essentials and Growth (setup, three months running, the first re-score), six months on In-House (two build months, three months running, the first re-score), then month to month with 30 days' notice. Pay the term up front and save $500 (Essentials or Growth) or $3,000 (In-House). Very large or multi-property situations are quoted individually. Project work (loyalty program design, guest database and email, website and booking engine rebuild, systems migration, booking-site terms renegotiation, paid media setup) is quoted on its own.
Software: no software is included in the fee. A revenue management system is required on every plan. Duetto is RHG's preferred system, and every client on every plan gets it at specially negotiated pricing because RHG is a contracted Duetto vendor and passes its vendor commission back to the client. The client holds the Duetto account; every rate plan, rule and piece of data belongs to the client. If a client already runs a revenue management system they prefer, RHG will consider working inside it.
Controls: the owner sets the floors and ceilings for every room type; nothing goes below the floor without sign-off; any change is reversed on request; every move is logged with its reason; results are reported against the market, not just last year, split into rate and occupancy, net of commission.
Call to action: Book The Modern Hotel Audit. https://ramirezhospitality.com/revenue-management

### 3. The Modern Hotel Plan ($6,000, flat, priced up front)
A feasibility study for anyone buying, building or opening a hotel under 50 rooms. Know the numbers before you buy, build, or open. Three questions in order: is the demand real, does the math work, what is the property worth (by income, by comparable sales and by cost, and which of the three the lender believes). The deliverable is the study, the working model, and a clear yes, no, or not at this price. A broker's pro forma is a sales document; the Plan is allowed to say no. The turnaround is stated on the call. Every Launch starts with a Plan.
Call to action: Book The Modern Hotel Plan. https://ramirezhospitality.com/feasibility-study

### The Modern Hotel Launch (quoted per project)
The hands-on hotel opening or reopening engagement: brand and budget to first guest, ten phases, on site nationwide. For the owner with a signed lease or purchase, a renovation under way, or an opening date and no one who has opened a hotel before. It also covers the reset for a property that is open and underperforming. Quoted per project after the Plan. A general manager runs a hotel that exists; an opening is a different job, ten phases in the right order, handed off to the manager at the end. The Subscription picks up once the hotel is open.
Call to action: Book an Opening Consultation. https://ramirezhospitality.com/openings

## Proof
- The Lincoln, Marfa, Texas: scored 41 out of 100, grade D, on a property guests love; $55,000 to $185,000 in annual revenue opportunity identified on a $444,000 base; guests paid $59 a night more on Expedia than on the hotel's own site.
- Paloma, Palm Springs: upscale boutique opening, year-one revenue $1.5M, featured in Travel & Leisure.
- Twist Hotel: distressed turnaround and reopening, Booking score 6.4 to 9.1, 60% direct booking rate.
- Limón, California: upscale boutique launch, featured in Modernism Magazine.
- Six funded hospitality projects with full pro formas and sensitivity scenarios.

## Common questions, answered
- Will you price me out of my own market? You set the floors and ceilings for every room type. Nothing goes below your floor without your sign-off, every change is logged with the reason, and any change is reversed on request.
- Software does this for a fraction of the price. We run the software for you and do what it cannot: work the booking sites as a cost line, price the wedding inquiry, keep your own website from being undercut. Compare the fee to your hours, not to the software.
- Do you take a cut? No. The fee on the page is the whole fee. Nothing is on commission.
- It's you, Adam. What if you get busy or sell? The method is the product and it lives in your own account. A second contact is named on every account. If you wanted to take it over tomorrow, you could.
- How will I know it was you and not the market? Results are reported against your market, not just against last year, split into rate and occupancy, net of commission. The baseline is fixed in the audit before anything changes.
- My broker already gave me a pro forma. A broker's pro forma is a sales document. The Plan answers three questions in order, from someone who has run the front desk and priced the rooms, and it is allowed to say no.
- I have a general manager for that. A general manager runs a hotel that exists. An opening is a different job: ten phases in the right order, from the name and the budget to the first guest, and it hands off to the manager at the end.
